sections.html:
A Sherman owner has three realistic paths: hire an agent, market the house alone, or take an investor's cash bid. Let the house's condition and your deadline decide. Sherman is the Grayson County seat on U.S. Highway 75, about seventy-five miles north of Dallas, so the buyer pool mixes commuters, local workers and investors. U.S. Highway 82 and State highways 11 and 56 also cross the city, which is worth a line in a listing aimed at commuters.

  • Agent: the most exposure, plus repair requests and a lender's schedule to sit through.
  • Going alone: you run the contract and buyer questions yourself, with a title company handling closing.
  • Cash bid: the house sells as it stands, which helps with a tenant, an inherited property or postponed repairs.

Before you talk to anyone, line up a lender payoff figure and the county's tax statement for your parcel.

Two county offices matter. Valuations come from the Grayson County Appraisal District (205 N Travis Street, 903-893-9673). The Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector (100 W Houston, 903-892-8297) sends and collects the bills.

The appraisal district's online database also shows the estimated tax on a parcel, which makes it the quickest check on what a buyer would carry. Use it too for values on nearby streets. An appraisal is a tax value, so a buyer's offer may land above or below it.

Four units tax a typical Sherman home. The City of Sherman's tax page prints each rate per $100 of assessed value as of January 1, 2025, and the city council adopted its own rate on September 2, 2025.

Rates change from year to year, so ask the Grayson County tax office what your latest bill carries before you quote a figure to a buyer.

Semiconductor work is the big local story. The city's home page features a 300mm wafer fab that has begun production and a $650 million indium phosphide fab expansion at a local optics plant. Those projects bring workers who need housing, and some want a simple, quick purchase near the plants. Strong interest does not erase the need for sensible pricing. Compare any offer against what similar Sherman houses actually closed for, and rely on sold-home records instead of headlines when you set an asking price.

Sherman has housing from many decades, so a buyer's inspector will look hard at roofs, foundations and wiring in anything old. A seller who holds records of updates has a real advantage. Collect permits, invoices and warranties before you list.

sections.h2: How Texas bills and penalizes property tax
sections.html:
Expect your bill near October 1 and a due date of January 31. A balance still open on February 1 turns delinquent, with a six percent charge and one percent interest added.

  • The lien and the valuation both date from January 1.
  • You may split the payment: half by November 30, the rest by June 30 of the next year.
  • Owners over 65 or disabled can pay in installments and may get a school tax ceiling.
  • A principal residence earns a $140,000 school homestead exemption, and those older owners get $60,000 more.

At closing the settlement statement divides this year's bill according to the closing date. Any earlier balance is paid out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Sherman buyers who pay cash can move fast, so be ready before the first offer. Request your lender's payoff figure and print the tax statement from the county. Look up your parcel in the appraisal district database to see the estimated tax and the value on file. Collect leases if the house is rented, and any city notices that are open against the property. Having these in one folder lets a buyer make a real offer instead of a guess.

  • Lender payoff figure and the latest tax statement.
  • Records of roof, foundation and wiring updates.
  • Leases and tenant contact details, if any.
  • Any open city notices.

Offers in Sherman differ in more than price. Ask each buyer for proof of funds and a closing date in writing. Find out who orders the title search and who pays for title and recording. Ask whether the offer assumes the house stays as is, and what happens if the title search turns up a lien or an old tax balance. If you have a tenant, ask whether the buyer will keep the lease or expects an empty house. When an investor knows your timeline, the choice often comes down to certainty over a slightly higher number.

A rundown house can still sell, but check with the city first. Sherman's Quality Neighborhoods Program targets blight and decay by removing substandard structures, either voluntarily with the owner's consent or through a court order.

If city notices are open against your house, resolve them or disclose them before listing, because a lender may decline a loan on a structure with violations. A cash buyer may accept the condition, though the bid will reflect repair or demolition costs. Neighborhood Services handles questions about specific properties.

Sherman deeds are recorded by the Grayson County Clerk. Before recording, a notary or other authorized officer has to acknowledge the signature.

Fees follow a statewide schedule with a flat charge for page one, a smaller one for later pages and some records charges. The title company will quote the total.

Unless the lease or the law lets you end it, a lease keeps running, so a buyer may purchase with the tenant in place. To end a tenancy in Texas you begin with a written notice to vacate, normally three days unless the lease says otherwise, and the case then moves to justice court.

  • The tenant gets served at least four days before trial.
  • An appeal to county court is due within five days of judgment.
  • A writ of possession becomes available six days after the final judgment.

Investors can plan around those timelines. Someone buying to live there will usually want the keys at closing.

Heirs have up to four years after a death to offer a Texas will for probate. If the estate owes nothing besides liens, a muniment of title may let them prove ownership without a full administration. A small estate affidavit covers estates worth up to $75,000, leaving out the homestead and exempt property.

Auctions are held on a month's first Tuesday, following at least 21 days' notice. A borrower can reinstate by paying the arrears within 20 days of the default notice. A sale before auction day can keep your equity intact.

faqs.a: Grayson County, where Sherman is the seat. The county appraisal district sets values, and the county tax assessor-collector sends the bills.

faqs.q: What city tax rate did Sherman adopt in 2025?
faqs.a: The city lists $0.508000 per $100 of assessed value, adopted September 2, 2025. For your current bill, check with the Grayson County tax office.

faqs.q: Do unpaid taxes stop a sale?
faqs.a: They do not stop it, but the lien rides with the house. The balance, penalties and interest must be paid at or before closing, and the settlement statement will show the amount.

faqs.q: Could the city's blight program touch my house?
faqs.a: It can, if the structure is substandard. Removal happens by consent or court order, and Neighborhood Services can answer questions about a particular address.

faqs.q: How fast can a Sherman house close?
faqs.a: A cash deal skips loan underwriting, so it can finish sooner than a financed one. Title work, probate or lien payoffs can still set the schedule, so get proof of funds and a closing date in writing.
